Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has named Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, as the Nigerian leader he would most like to seek advice from, dead or alive. Makinde made the remark during a special rooftop conversation with Channels Television’s Kayode Okikiolu in a video shared on X on Monday, where he was asked which Nigerian leader he would like to speak with. “The Nigerian leader, dead or alive, I would like to speak to is Baba Nnamdi Azikiwe,” he said. The governor explained that although he held the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo in high regard, he was particularly interested in understanding the decisions Azikiwe made at a critical point in Nigeria’s history. He said Azikiwe was at the centre of a crucial moment in the country’s history and that he wanted to understand the thinking behind a decision he believed Nigeria was still grappling with 66 years later. I would love to really have an insight and ask him, ‘Papa, how did you get here?’” The conversation comes as Makinde pursues his presidential ambition on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement ahead of the 2027 general election. He is expected to run with former Director-General of the Department of State Services, Lawal Daura, as his running mate. 2027: Tinubu woos Igbo, recalls 2023 defeat in Lagos Okpebholo promises third Benin flyover if Tinubu wins re-election APC disowns letter asking INEC to ensure Tinubu’s 2027 victory Makinde’s admiration for Azikiwe is not new. At the 12th Annual Zik Lecture Series in Awka, Anambra State, on November 16, 2023, he praised the late nationalist’s commitment to Nigerian unity and argued that the country needed restructuring to promote fairness and strengthen its federal system. He had described Azikiwe as a dynamic leader who was willing to adapt to changing political realities, adding that Nigeria should focus on building a structure that works for all its federating units.
